news.title: Flamingos: Why FIFA will not reward U-17 Women's World Cup champions with money
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Mark YEN.com.gh as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed! Nigeria's Flamingos have created history by becoming the first African nation to claim the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup title, defeating Japan 2-1 in the final in Rabat, Morocco. However, the groundbreaking achievement will not be accompanied by any official prize money from FIFA. FIFA classifies its youth tournaments as developmental competitions, with the focus placed on player growth and international exposure rather than financial incentives.

news.title: Japan coach Shirai breaks silence after Flamingos win FIFA U-17 World Cup title
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Mark Legit.ng as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed! Japan head coach Sadayoshi Shirai has broken his silence after his side fell 2-1 to Nigeria's Flamingos in the final of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, conceding that Nigeria's physical strength and speed were decisive factors in the outcome. The defeat made history as Nigeria became the first African nation to win the competition, completing one of the most dramatic runs the tournament has ever seen. Speaking to FIFA's official website after the final whistle, Shirai was candid about the challenge his players faced against the Flamingos.

news.title: Former NFF Official Credits Tinubu Administration for Flamingos' World Cup Victory
news.lede: Former Nigeria Football Federation First Vice-President, Seyi Akinwunmi, has described the Flamingos’ historic FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup triumph as evidence of the benefits of sustained grassroots investment and the sports reforms of President Bola Tinubu’s administration. Akinwunmi, a former chairman of the Lagos State Football Association, spoke in Lagos after Nigeria defeated Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final in Morocco to become the first African nation to win the competition. He said the achievement was not accidental but reflected the importance of deliberate investment in youth development and the creation of opportunities for young female footballers.“. This victory did not happen by chance.

news.title: Nigeria make history: Morocco send a strong message ahead of the 2030 World Cup
news.lede: Morocco continued testing its organisational capabilities and sporting and logistical infrastructure by hosting the Women's Under-17 World Cup. The tournament concluded in the capital Rabat with Nigeria crowned champions for the first time in their history, after a 2-1 victory over Japan. It marked a new stage in the kingdom's preparations to host the 2030 World Cup in partnership with Spain and Portugal.Spanish newspaper "Sport" reported that the tournament's importance went beyond the sporting competition, offering Morocco an additional opportunity to test its facilities, organisational mechanisms, delegation management and logistical operations as part of the plan to prepare for football's showpiece in 2030. The kingdom has secured the right to organise five consecutive editions of the tournament from 2025 to 2029.

news.title: Barça supplies seven of Spain’s 21 players for the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar
news.lede: Barcelona has more players than any other club in David Cubillo's Spain squad for the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar. The selection gives La Masia a central role in Spain's campaign in Doha.David Cubillo has leaned heavily on La Masia for Spain’s Under-17 World Cup campaign. The coach’s list includes Raúl Expósito, Sergi Mayans, Baba Kourouma, Jordi Pesquer, Ebrima Tunkara, Roberto Tomás and Iu Martínez.Beyond the defenders, Tunkara and Tomás are among the midfielders. Martínez is listed in attack.

Nigeria's Flamingos created history by becoming the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, beating Japan in a memorable final. Yet, despite the magnitude of the achievement, the team will walk away without a single kobo in official prize money from FIFA. Oluebube Umejiaku was the hero of the final, scoring a stunning individual goal in the second half to settle the contest.

news.title: Flamingos receive big cash reward after winning FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Find it fast with our new search feature at Legit.ng! Nigeria's Flamingos have received a $50,000 cash reward after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Rabat, Morocco, becoming the first African nation to win the tournament. The gift was presented by Alhaji Saleh Ahmadu, a sponsor of the National Sports Commission, at a reception held in Rabat on Saturday night in honour of the victorious squad. National Sports Commission Chairman Shehu Dikko and Director-General Bukola Olopade hosted the event, which was also attended by the Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi.

news.title: 'No withdrawals' as Poland prepares to host FIFA tournament amid Infantino backlash
news.lede: It will be the first FIFA competition since UEFA voted to support a boycott of FIFA events. Hosts Poland said on Tuesday that preparations for next month's Under-20 Women's World Cup remain on schedule, as the tournament prepares to become the first FIFA event staged amid the backlash against global football chief Gianni Infantino. It will be the first FIFA competition since UEFA's 55 member associations unanimously voted to support a boycott of FIFA events after Infantino proposed and then abandoned a plan to carve off the commercial rights to the World Cup and sell 20% of them to private investors to raise about $4.2 billion. That triggered a massive football governance dispute.
